extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, computer scientists, and mathematics educators seeking information on 1996 conferences, workshops, courses, and their submission/registration procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Collects the procedural requirements, deadlines, eligibility, and submission/registration details for conferences, workshops, and advanced courses listed in the Notices of the AMS (1996). Focus is on how and when to submit abstracts/papers, apply for grants, register, and what participant expectations/limits exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts to Organizing Committee (May 20, 1996)
rubrics_metrics.description: be sent to the Organizing Committee by May 20, 1996, by post or e-mail. The abstracts of communications will also be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send correspondence to L. A. Uvarova at Dept. of Information and Applied Mathematics, Tver State Technical Univ.; includes postal address, teletype, e-mail, and fax contact; instruction: (in the left upper corner write: Box 3267).

rubrics_metrics.name: CRM Advanced Courses — grants, registration, accommodation (Geometry & Physics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRM can offer a limited number of grants covering the registration fee. The deadline for applying is March 20, 1996. Registration: Fee: 20.000 pta. Deadline: April 15, 1996. Payment for registration and accommodation should be made by April 15, 1996. Accommodation: The CRM can offer accommodation from July 1 to July 12 (11 nights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See registration form for more details; information and contacts provided (WWW, ftp, mail). Grants are limited — apply by stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutative Algebra Summer School — short talks and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants interested in giving a short talk (30 min.) should submit an abstract by the end of February 1996. Depending on the numbers, the coordinators may be forced to make a selection among those offering a talk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator names provided. Those offering talks must meet the abstract deadline; selection may be competitive if many applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRM Commutative Algebra — grants, registration & accommodation (Summer School)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRM can offer a limited number of grants. The deadline for applying is March 31, 1996. Registration: Fee: 20.000 pta. Payment for registration and accommodation should be made by May 10, 1996. Accommodation: The CRM can offer accommodation from July 15 to July 27 (12 nights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should obtain and return the registration form before the stated deadlines; contact info (WWW/ftp/mail/fax) given for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ATLAST Linear Algebra Workshops — eligibility, application deadline, and participant limit
rubrics_metrics.description: All teachers of undergraduate linear algebra courses at colleges or universities in the USA are invited to apply for the ATLAST workshops. The deadline for applications is March 21, 1996. Late applications will be accepted on a space available basis. Each workshop will be limited to thirty participants. A screening committee will review applications and notify applicants of its decisions by the beginning of April.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late applications considered only if space remains. Contact S. J. Leon (ATLAST Project Director) for instructions on applying and further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ATLAST Workshop — participant expectations and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop participants will learn about existing software for linear algebra and will be trained in the use of the MATLAB software package. Attendees will design classroom lessons that incorporate computer software making use of ATLAST materials developed in previous workshops. These materials will be included in the forthcoming 'ATLAST Book of Computer Exercises' (Prentice-Hall, Fall, 1996). Participants will also learn to design computer exercises and lab projects for inclusion in the ATLAST database and possible inclusion in future editions of the ATLAST book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are expected to actively prepare classroom lessons and software-based exercises; materials produced may be published or included in project databases/books.

rubrics_metrics.name: LICS (Eleventh Annual IEEE Symposium on Logic in Computer Science) — paper submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission Deadline: Papers must be received by December 13; late submissions will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complete call for papers is available from the listed URL/FTP; adhere strictly to the December 13 receipt deadline as late submissions are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICECCS / Engineering of Complex Computer Systems — submission types, length limits, copies, and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Both long (under 5,000 words) and short (under 2,500 words) submissions are welcome, including presentations of complete work, summaries of work in progress, position statements, exhibit proposals, tutorial proposals. A submission may address any combination of research, technology or applications within the ECCS area. All submissions should be made, in eight copies, by April 15, 1996, to: A. Stoyenko. Authors will be notified by July 15, 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective participants are encouraged to contact and discuss possible submissions with appropriate chairs. There is also contact information for exhibit proposals and research prototypes (T. Bihari). Follow the 8-copy postal submission requirement and the April 15 deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: GF-96 (Generalized Functions) — registration and abstract/publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Call for Papers: Abstracts of the lectures will be published before, the Proceedings after the Conference. Deadline: The registration form should be sent to the organizers by March 1, 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organized by the Institute of Mathematics, Novi Sad; contact details (tel./fax/e-mail) provided. Abstracts will be published in advance and full proceedings after the meeting — ensure timely submission of registration form by March 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESF Workshop (Journées Numériques de Besançon) — abstracts deadline and workshop theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline: For submission of abstracts: March 1, 1996. Theme: Free boundary problems and shape optimization are two very active fields; the aim of this meeting is to take stock of these subjects and to develop more particularly the numerical aspects (methods and algorithms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers and secretariat contact information provided. Key Words include numerical analysis, free boundaries, shape optimization; submit abstracts by March 1 to be considered for the program.
